newsitem.title: JAPAN: OLYMPICS-CROSS COUNTRY SKIER TO WIN FIRST GOLD MEDAL IN NAGANO.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-CROSS COUNTRY SKIER TO WIN FIRST GOLD MEDAL IN NAGANO.

text.p: The first gold medal at next February's Nagano winter Olympics will now be won by a women's cross country skier instead of the men's downhill champion.

The Nagano Organising Committee (NAOC) said on Wednesday the International Ski Federation had complained that a 1.30 p.m start to the women's 15 km cross country event on February 8 was too late in the day to ensure consistent snow conditions.

Under a revised programme, which needs to be approved by an International Olympic Committee executive board meeting in Monaco on May 19, cross country events will instead start between 9 a.m and noon.

Under the new scenario, the women's 15 km cross country event will start at 9 a.m. and finish around 10 a.m. while the men's downhill, one of the Games' glamour events, will not be decided until about 12.30.
However the medal ceremonies for both events will take place at the same time later in the day back in Nagano, about 30 km from the ski slopes.

NAOC also proposes slightly different starting times in mogul skiing, the bobsleigh and speed skating to take account of suggestions made after a series of World Cup events held in the Nagano area earlier this year.
